title.narrative: APSM II Regional Dialogues on the Future of Afghanistan 2021-2022
APSM II Regional Dialogues on the Future of Afghanistan 2021-2022

description.narrative:
Projektet har för avsikt att generera konsensus mellan regionala intressenter om hur Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, och Kyrgyzstan kan använda sitt inflytande för att stötta de intra-afghanska fredsförhandlingarna att nå ett slut på den 40-åriga konflikten. Nyckelaktiviteter inkluderar en serie av dialoger mellan inflytelserika aktörer från Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan och Afghanistan för att diskutera säkerhetsgarantier och mekanismer för samarbete under den afghanska fredsprocessen, och hur länderna kan arbeta för ett närmre ekonomiskt samarbete på bilaterala och regionala nivåer.
Projektet finansieras genom EU Afghanistan Peace Support Mechansim II (EU APSM II) som är en EU- och Sida-finansierad mekanism med avsikt att stödja en inkluderande fredsprocess i Afghanistan.

The aim of the project is to generate consensus among regional stakeholders on how Afghanistan’s Central Asian neighbours can use their influence in support of the Afghan peace negotiations to achieve a just and enduring end to the 40-year-old Afghan conflict. The key activity involves a series of dialogues between influential actors from the countries to discuss the security concerns of the countries during the ongoing Afghan peace process and following the conclusion of intra-Afghan negotiations, to clarify the security guarantees and mechanisms of cooperation the countries see as necessary under both scenarios, and to exchange insights and ideas on issues and questions of longer-term significance with a focus on how Afghanistan and Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Kyrgyzstan can work together to realise closer economic cooperation at the bilateral and regional levels.
The project will be financed as part of the EU Afghanistan Peace Support Mechanism II (EU APSM II) which is a mechanism co-funded by EU and Sida aimed at supporting an inclusive peace process in Afghanistan.

HAS carried out 3 online dialogue events (à 2,5 hour each), gathering various experts from Afghanistan, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Turkey and Uzbekistan, as well as a few European participants. To inform participants and animate dialogues, each of the dialogue sessions were preceded by discussion papers that detailed the current situation in Afghanistan as well as the challenges facing the country and the people, and the implications of the evolving situation for the region. The discussion papers were jointly drafted by HAS, and posed questions based on the project proposal as well as current themes about issues facing the country. The dialogue events were the following: 1. The first dialogue session was carried out on 31 March 2022 and focused on the issues of a) Threats and Opportunities for Stability in Afghanistan and the Region, and b) Afghan and Regional Views on "Inclusivity" in Afghanistan. 2. The second dialogue session was carried out on 28 April 2022 and focused on the issues of a) Response to Humanitarian Crisis and the Region, and b) Counter Terrorism and Transnational Security Challenges. 3. The third and last dialogue session was carried out on 9 June 2022 and focused on a) Regional Perspectives on the Taliban De Facto Government Engagement, Recognition or Isolation, and b) Rising Insecurity Transnational Militant Groups in Afghanistan, Implications for the People of Afghanistan and the Region. Initially, the plan was to host the meeting in person Istanbul but due to political reasons the event needed to be moved online.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
